stories.title: Trump says he ordered Army not to detonate lead azide in Iowa without court approval
stories.summary: Monday's post on Truth Social is the first time the president himself has spoken out on the Army's planned detonation of nearly five tons of lead azide.

stories.title: Winter weather raises risk from unstable lead azide stockpile, expert says
stories.summary: A chemistry professor says freezing conditions could increase the risk of an uncontrolled explosion, adding urgency to the Army's planned detonation.

stories.title: Gov. Reynolds orders flags to half-staff in honor of Wally E. Horn
stories.summary: Horn served for 46 consecutive years in the Iowa Legislature and is Iowa's longest-serving legislator.

stories.title: US Army to detonate lead azide Wednesday. What Iowa leaders are saying
stories.summary: Army officials said the material has become increasingly unstable and poses a growing risk if left in storage.

stories.title: Gov. Reynolds' annual turkey pardoning event will not happen this year, office says
stories.summary: The Governor will still issue a proclamation, her office shared in an email.

stories.title: What is lead azide? Army plans controlled detonation of hazardous explosives in Iowa
stories.summary: The Army plans to destroy 5 tons of unstable lead azide explosives at an Iowa ammunition plant, despite legal attempts to stop the detonation.

stories.title: Turek calls for investigation as environmental groups, state prepare for Army detonation
stories.summary: Sen.-elect Turek seeks answers on Middletown's lead azide stockpile as environmental groups push for protections and Iowa prepares for detonation.

stories.title: US Army announces controlled detonation now scheduled for Wednesday
stories.summary: The Army said the delay will allow for "optimal weather conditions and all mitigation measures to be emplaced."

stories.title: TIMELINE: What we know about the lead azide detonation since Army discovered it in March
stories.summary: The Army found 68 barrels, or nearly five tons, of deteriorated lead azide back in March. What has happened in the months since?

stories.title: Noon Sunday deadline set in Iowa Army blast challenge; Fort Madison says detonation could come Monday or Tuesday
stories.summary: Fort Madison says the Iowa Army detonation could happen Monday or Tuesday. An appeals court ordered a response to the stay request by noon Sunday.

stories.title: Army's planned lead azide detonation for Wednesday in limbo after Trump announcement
stories.summary: The Army had said it would invoke an emergency exemption to federal hazardous waste regulations that would allow it to proceed without the EPA's emergency permit.

stories.title: Officials respond to apartment fire in Johnston Saturday afternoon
stories.summary: No injuries were reported, according to authorities.
